evidenceAudit.scope: Acute, staggered, modified-release and repeated supratherapeutic paracetamol (acetaminophen) poisoning in adults and children in India: risk assessment, activated charcoal, acetylcysteine and liver-unit referral. Built on the Australian and New Zealand paracetamol guideline (MJA 2020) with the ICMR Acute Liver Failure STW (July 2020) acetylcysteine regimen.
findings: Toxic thresholds (10 g or 200 mg/kg, whichever is less), repeated supratherapeutic ingestion thresholds, two-bag acetylcysteine doses and caps, charcoal 50 g, modified-release rules, children's liquid ingestion pathway, stopping criteria and liver transplant unit referral criteria checked against MJA 2020 Boxes 1–8.

The three-step acetylcysteine regimen (150 mg/kg over 1 hour, 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, 100 mg/kg over 16 hours) for drug-induced acute liver failure checked against the ICMR Acute Liver Failure STW (July 2020).
unverifiedSections: No Indian paracetamol-poisoning guideline was opened; the MJA 2020 guideline is the main source, and MJA notes some nomograms swap units, so check mg/L vs μmol/L.

Two-bag acetylcysteine is listed as preferred because it is the overdose-specific regimen; the ICMR three-step regimen is the Indian acute liver failure regimen. The clinician chooses by local protocol.
A paediatric activated charcoal dose is not given in the opened sources.
The treatment nomogram line values are not reproduced; use the nomogram in the MJA guideline.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Paracetamol is safe at therapeutic doses (up to 60 mg/kg/day, maximum 4 g/day in adults) but overdose saturates normal conjugation, so more drug is converted to the toxic metabolite NAPQI. When hepatic glutathione is used up, NAPQI causes centrilobular liver necrosis, which may progress to acute liver failure, kidney injury and death. Early patients often have no symptoms. Acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and is almost fully protective when started within 8 hours of ingestion; it still helps when started late or after liver injury (MJA 2020). Risk is judged from the dose ingested, the paracetamol concentration on the nomogram for single immediate-release ingestions, and ALT.
keyMechanisms: Overdose saturates glucuronidation and sulfation, so more paracetamol becomes NAPQI.
NAPQI binds liver proteins once glutathione is exhausted, causing centrilobular necrosis.
Acetylcysteine restores glutathione and detoxifies NAPQI.
Liver failure leads to coagulopathy, hypoglycaemia, encephalopathy and kidney injury.

symptoms: Often none in the first 24 hours
Right upper quadrant pain at 24–72 hours
Confusion and jaundice in liver failure
physicalSigns: Jaundice, encephalopathy, bleeding in late presentation
redFlags: INR above 3.0 at 48 hours or above 4.5 at any time (MJA 2020)
pH below 7.3 or lactate above 3 mmol/L (MJA 2020)
Encephalopathy, hypoglycaemia, systolic BP below 80 mmHg (MJA 2020)
Ingestion of 50 g or more, or 1 g/kg or more: seek toxicology advice (MJA 2020)
precipitants: Repeated excess doses for pain or fever

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Gradual onset, viral serology positive, no ingestion history.

differentials.condition: Other hepatotoxic drugs (anti-TB drugs, herbal products)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Preceding shock; very high ALT that falls quickly.
Reduced consciousness early is not caused by paracetamol alone.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 10 g or more, or 200 mg/kg or more, whichever is less; doses over more than 2 hours (staggered) count as acute.
10 g or 200 mg/kg in 24 hours; 12 g or 300 mg/kg in 48 hours; or therapeutic doses for over 48 hours with abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting (whichever is less).
Only for a single immediate-release ingestion with a known time, from 4 hours after ingestion.
Suspected ingestion above 200 mg/kg: concentration at 2 hours; below 150 mg/L needs no acetylcysteine.

clinicalManagement.title: Risk assess
actions: Estimate dose in mg/kg and time; classify as acute, staggered, modified-release or repeated supratherapeutic (MJA Box 1).
Contact a poisons centre or toxicologist for 50 g or 1 g/kg or more, concentration over triple the line, ALT above 1000 U/L or IV paracetamol errors (MJA 2020).

clinicalManagement.title: Decontaminate
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Within 2 hours (4 hours for over 30 g or modified-release)
actions: Activated charcoal 50 g for an awake, cooperative adult within 2 hours of a toxic dose, or 4 hours if over 30 g (MJA Box 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Start acetylcysteine
actions: Immediate-release: treat if level on or above the nomogram line; start at once if a level cannot be obtained within 8 hours (MJA Box 3).
Modified-release 10 g or 200 mg/kg or more: start at once and give a full course whatever the level (MJA Box 4).
Repeated supratherapeutic: start if paracetamol above 20 mg/L or ALT above 50 U/L (MJA Box 5).

clinicalManagement.title: Stop or continue
actions: Stop when ALT or AST falling, INR below 2.0 and clinically well; for modified-release or above double the line, paracetamol must also be below 10 mg/L (MJA Box 8).
If continuing: review and test at least every 12 hours.

clinicalManagement.title: Liver failure
actions: Refer to a liver transplant unit for INR above 3.0 at 48 hours or above 4.5, creatinine above 200 μmol/L, pH below 7.3, lactate above 3 mmol/L, systolic BP below 80 mmHg, hypoglycaemia or encephalopathy (MJA 2020).
Do not give clotting factors unless bleeding (MJA 2020).
Psychiatric assessment before discharge after self-poisoning.

medicationPlan.note: Thresholds and the two-bag acetylcysteine regimen are from MJA 2020; the three-step regimen is from the ICMR Acute Liver Failure STW (2020). India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Paracetamol poisoning in Indian emergency practice.
learningObjectives: Classify the ingestion and decide on treatment.
Know when to stop and when to refer to a liver unit.
keyPoints: Toxic: 10 g or 200 mg/kg, whichever is less.
Start acetylcysteine if the level will not be back by 8 hours.
Stop: ALT falling, INR below 2, well.
INR above 3 at 48 hours: liver unit.
pitfalls: Using the nomogram for staggered or modified-release ingestion.
Stopping because the level is low while ALT rises.
